review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its simp interface only. The only simp attributes are on `IsLipschitzParametrizable.empty` and `IsLipschitzParametrizable.singleton`. Both have closed-form conclusions of the form `IsLipschitzParametrizable d ∅` and `IsLipschitzParametrizable d {x}`. They have no hypotheses, they don't rewrite anything, and they can't loop. The simp calls inside the file are the `empty` case of `biUnion_finset`, which uses the simp-tagged `empty`, and a few `simpa` calls on cube-coordinate goals. I found no competing rules and no rewrite in an unsuitable direction. `isLipschitzParametrizable_iff` is `Iff.rfl` on a definition. Tagging it simp would unfold the definition everywhere and make the stated normal form worse, so it is correctly left unannotated. The closure lemmas (`mono`, `union`, `image`, `prod`, `finite`) all have hypotheses that are themselves parametrizability facts. They are better used as `exact` or dot-notation terms than as simp lemmas, and I found no use that needs simp to discharge them. I did not run Lean and did not search other files for downstream simp uses of these lemmas, so a downstream problem is still possible but unevidenced.
